answer: Each new identity must complete a sequential memory-hard forge that builds a private spiral of intermediate states bound to the epoch seed; the states cannot be checkpointed or shared across clones. Verification at the jetty of admission checks the final digest in constant time, but an attacker spinning up N identities pays N full sequential working-sets in RAM and wall-clock. Parallel farms still burn linear capital per fake, so the marginal alias costs more than its expected reward.
